purpose: Illustrated proposed workflow, not experimental evidence

prompts.name: task-start
prompts.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: wide 16:9 hero scene and canonical reference for a robotics solution storyboard on a Vietnamese engineering project website.
Primary request: a polished, technically legible 3D editorial illustration of a generic research humanoid performing tabletop pick-and-place, not a photograph of a real experiment.
Scene: clean light gray robotics lab. One fixed humanoid standing behind a rectangular matte white worktable. A single small yellow rectangular rigid component on the left half of the worktable. A shallow gray 2-by-3 compartment tray on the right half; its front-left target compartment has a subtle green outline. No other loose objects. Warm neutral lab backdrop, minimal distractions.
Robot: consistent white and graphite humanoid, head with a dark camera visor, graphite joint housings, simple two-finger parallel grippers on both hands. Torso upright and fixed, one active arm reaches toward the yellow component, the other arm rests down. Realistic plausible arm proportions and joints. Not a commercial brand, no logos.
Composition: wide landscape 16:9, three-quarter front view with the whole robot upper body, active gripper, yellow part and all tray compartments visible; fixed camera looking slightly down onto tabletop. The active gripper is OPEN and approaching the yellow part but not holding it. The yellow part is clearly outside the tray. This is the start state, NOT task success.
Style: clean premium educational 3D illustration, restrained material detail, soft shadows, crisp geometry, pale blue ambient accents, unmistakably a designed illustration. Enough visual contrast to see gripper tips and part. No text, no typography, no arrows, no UI, no charts, no floating holograms, no watermarks. Keep the task geometry especially clear. Website captions and diagram labels will be separate HTML.
Constraints: exactly one robot, one yellow component, one 6-compartment tray. Preserve physical separation between gripper and component. Use this as a consistent canonical scene for subsequent variations.

prompts.name: visual-failure
prompts.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit target: the supplied canonical robotics storyboard scene. Keep the EXACT same white/graphite humanoid identity, same camera composition, worktable, yellow rectangular component, gray 2-by-3 tray with front-left green target, and lab. Change only lighting and the active gripper pose to depict a VISUAL FAILURE illustration: the task workspace has a deep cast shadow and dimmer cool lighting, yet component remains visible. Active gripper is CLOSED EMPTY over bare tabletop roughly 12 cm to the LEFT of the yellow component, clearly missing it. Yellow component remains in its original place outside tray. Other arm at rest. Robot pose plausible, fingers short and parallel as original. Failure unambiguous from physical separation. No text, arrows, UI or labels. Educational 3D designed illustration, not real test evidence. Landscape 16:9.

prompts.name: contact-failure
prompts.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit target: supplied canonical robotics storyboard scene. Preserve exact robot identity, lab, camera, tabletop, gray 2-by-3 tray and front-left green target. Show CONTACT FAILURE: active arm has lifted and moved halfway toward tray, gripper above tabletop near center, jaws slightly separated; the SINGLE yellow component is visibly falling just below the empty gripper, tilted in mid-air, still far from target tray. One small subtle motion streak can convey downward fall but no arrows, text, UI or labels. Original normal bright neutral lighting. Other arm at rest. Physically plausible robot proportions. Clear separation so user can see that component slipped. Educational 3D illustration, not a real experiment. 16:9 landscape.

prompts.name: task-success
prompts.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit target: supplied canonical robotics storyboard scene. Preserve exact white/graphite robot identity, same lab/camera/table/gray 2-by-3 tray. Depict EXPECTED end state of the proposed pick-and-place: the ONE yellow rectangular component rests fully INSIDE the front-left green-outlined compartment. No yellow part remains elsewhere on tabletop. Active gripper is OPEN and withdrawing 15 cm above that compartment, not holding or touching the yellow component. Other arm at rest, torso fixed. Same bright neutral lighting as original. All six compartments remain intact. Educational 3D illustration, NOT evidence of trained robot performance. 16:9 landscape, no text, arrows, UI, logos or watermarks.

prompts.name: human-demo
prompts.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Supporting reference: supplied canonical robotics scene only for EXACT same lab worktable, yellow rectangular component and gray six-compartment tray, lighting and 3D visual style. New scene: a human operator in a plain dark blue shirt (torso only, no face required) performs the same pick-and-place behind the same table in place of the robot. One hand holding the ONE yellow component just above the front-left green-outlined target compartment, other hand at rest. Clean physically plausible five-finger hand. Show an unobtrusive small chest-mounted camera on the human to suggest egocentric collection. Same 16:9 tabletop framing. No robot in this scene. Educational 3D illustration, no text, arrows, UI, logos or watermarks.
